reviewNotes: ADMIT-BACKSTAGE. Current first-party O2 data cleanly separates credit validity from SIM validity: the prepaid card is valid 12 months after the last top-up, while 300–499 CZK credit itself lasts six months. Current low-entry GO starter is 99 CZK with 100 CZK credit.

events.outcome: A 300–499 CZK top-up gives only six months of credit validity, but O2 separately states the prepaid SIM/card itself remains valid for 12 months from the last top-up. Do not confuse credit expiry with number/SIM expiry.

data.acquisitionSummary: Current O2 GO na den prepaid starter is listed at 99 CZK with 100 CZK preloaded credit. O2 sells additional prepaid variants; this route uses the current low-entry GO prepaid baseline.

keep.action: Top up at least the current self-service minimum of 300 CZK before 12 months since the last top-up. O2 states the prepaid card itself is valid 12 months from the last top-up. A 300–499 CZK top-up credit balance expires after six months, but that shorter credit-validity period is not the SIM-validity period.

data.chinaActivation: Overseas-first acquisition/activation is not established in this review.
data.kyc: A mandatory identity/KYC requirement was not established from the reviewed current O2 prepaid surface; do not infer either KYC-free or foreign-passport support from absence of a notice.
data.payment: O2 supports online top-up; exact foreign-card acceptance is not reconciled.
data.roamingSms: EU and non-EU roaming pricing exists; long-term incoming-SMS/OTP reliability is unverified.
data.refund: O2 documents prepaid credit rules; refund conditions are not reconciled here.
data.tariffSummary: 99 CZK GO starter; 300 CZK minimum self top-up; SIM validity is 12 months from last top-up.
guideSteps: Acquire a current O2 GO prepaid SIM.
Before 12 months from the last top-up, top up at least 300 CZK.
Treat the six-month validity of 300–499 CZK credit as credit expiry, not as the SIM/number expiry date.
